title: Week 23
subtitle: The glucose test is next. It is the last big screening before the third trimester.

baby.size: About the size of a grapefruit
baby.development: The baby can hear your voice clearly now and may startle at loud sounds. The lungs are developing blood vessels. Skin is still thin and translucent, and fat is starting to fill it out.

you.body: Your uterus is about an inch and a half above your belly button. You may have more Braxton Hicks tightenings. Your belly button may flatten or pop out, and it goes back after birth.
you.mind: The third trimester is close. If you have been putting off the practical planning, this is a good week for it — energy tends to dip again later.

coreActions.title: Have the glucose test
coreActions.why: Gestational diabetes usually has no symptoms. Finding it means it can be managed, which lowers the risk of a large baby and delivery complications.
coreActions.detail: You drink a sweet drink, wait an hour, and have a blood draw. Do not fast unless they tell you to. If the result is high, the next step is a longer test — a high screening result is not a diagnosis. About 1 in 10 pregnant people have gestational diabetes, and most manage it with food and monitoring.

options.label: The one-hour test
options.detail: The usual first step. No fasting at most practices.

options.label: The two-hour test
options.detail: Some practices start here. You fast beforehand.

coreActions.title: Learn the signs of preterm labor
coreActions.why: Preterm labor can be stopped or slowed if it is caught early. Knowing the signs is the difference between calling and waiting.
coreActions.detail: Regular contractions that get closer together, a low heavy feeling in the pelvis, a change in discharge, a gush of fluid, or backache that does not go away. If any of these happen before 37 weeks, call your OB rather than waiting for the next appointment. Calling and being wrong is fine.

options.label: Read the signs once
options.detail: Ten minutes now is worth it. You will remember more than you think.

options.label: Save the triage number
options.detail: Put it in your phone under a name you will find at 2am.

coreActions.skipIf: You already know the signs and have the number saved.

coreActions.title: Start a hospital bag, and leave it half-packed
coreActions.why: You may need it at 34 weeks, not 40. A bag that is mostly ready is better than one that is perfect and unpacked.
coreActions.detail: The useful list is short: ID and insurance card, phone charger with a long cable, comfortable clothes, toiletries, snacks, a going-home outfit for you and one for the baby, and a car seat in the car. The hospital provides most of the rest. Pack your partner a bag too.

options.label: Use a hospital's list
options.detail: Most publish one. It is shorter than the internet's version.

options.label: Write your own
options.detail: Ten items, one bag. Add as you think of things.

alsoKnow.title: A popping belly button is temporary
alsoKnow.body: The uterus pushes it out. It goes back after birth, though it may look different. A small hernia is possible and usually harmless — mention it at a visit.

alsoKnow.title: Braxton Hicks are practice, not progress
alsoKnow.body: They are irregular, they do not get stronger, and they usually stop if you change position or drink water. Real contractions get closer together and do not stop.

alsoKnow.title: Your feet may grow, and not only from swelling
alsoKnow.body: Relaxin loosens ligaments, and some people go up half a size permanently. Buy shoes that fit now rather than hoping.

redFlags.text: A gush or steady trickle of fluid from the vagina
A clear change in your baby's usual movement

appointments.label: Glucose screening test
appointments.note: About an hour. Ask whether to fast.
